criteria.title: Resource-Based Authorization & Ownership (CMP-07)
criteria.description: CampaignOwnershipRequirement : IAuthorizationRequirement and CampaignOwnershipHandler : AuthorizationHandler<CampaignOwnershipRequirement, Campaign> are registered and invoked via IAuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync after loading the campaign. CampaignManager creates campaigns (POST /campaigns) and modifies or deletes only their own campaigns (PUT and DELETE /campaigns/{id}), while Admin manages all campaigns. Modifying or deleting another manager's campaign returns 404 Campaign.NotFound, not 403. A request without a token to a protected endpoint returns 401. Ownership is checked in two layers (policy/role in the API, then an ownership check inside the handler — SRS §6.3), and the owner is taken from the token rather than the request body. GET /campaigns/mine returns the manager's own campaigns in all statuses, paged, with both-language fields.

criteria.title: Donations Module: Creation, Lists, and Stub (DON-01 to DON-06)
criteria.description: POST /campaigns/{campaignId}/donations with body { "amount": 25.00 } is available to Donor, Campaign Manager, and Admin, creates a donation with Pending status, and returns 201 Created with a Location header. A campaign that is not Active or whose EndDate has passed returns 409 Campaign.NotActive, and an amount outside the DonationOptions bounds (default 1.00 to 10,000.00) returns 422 Donation.AmountOutOfRange. GET /donations/mine returns only the current user's donations (amount, date, status, campaign title), paged. GET /donations/{id} is for the owner or Admin, and another user's donation returns 404 Donation.NotFound. GET /admin/donations is Admin-only with filters status, campaignId, donorId, from, and to. POST /admin/donations/{id}/mark-succeeded is Admin-only, a donation that is not Pending returns 409 Donation.InvalidState, and the endpoint is clearly marked as temporary to be removed in Sprint 5.

criteria.title: Atomic Success Flow, Concurrency, and Receipt Number (DON-07, DON-08)
criteria.description: Transitioning the donation to Succeeded runs inside one transaction (a single SaveChangesAsync through the UoW or an explicit BeginTransactionAsync): status Succeeded, CompletedAt from TimeProvider, ReceiptNumber, adding the amount to RaisedAmount, transitioning the campaign to Completed when RaisedAmount >= GoalAmount, then commit. The rules live inside the entities rather than directly modifying RaisedAmount from outside. Two concurrent donation successes are both counted: RowVersion with retry on DbUpdateConcurrencyException, or an atomic ExecuteUpdateAsync. ReceiptNumber uses the format DN-{year}-{6 digits} (e.g., DN-2026-000042) and is unique under concurrency (Database Sequence or Unique Index with retry — SRS §9.4), not MAX + 1 or an in-memory counter. A late payment on an expired or completed campaign is accepted and recorded as Succeeded with a warning via ILogger.

criteria.title: Pagination, Filtering & Sorting (CMP-08)
criteria.description: A generic PagedList<T> returns the shape { items, page, pageSize, totalCount, totalPages } (SRS §6.8), with a default page size of 20 and maximum of 50. Pagination is performed at the database level via Skip and Take on IQueryable before execution, and entire tables are not loaded into memory (no ToList before Skip, and totalCount is the total count). Applied across GET /campaigns, GET /campaigns/success-stories, GET /campaigns/mine, GET /donations/mine, and GET /admin/donations. The public campaign list searches TitleAr or TitleEn depending on the request language, filters by categoryId and status, and sorts via a whitelist only (endDate, raisedAmount, and createdAt, ascending or descending) without constructing column names from user input.

criteria.title: Caching: In-Memory Then Redis with Invalidation (CMP-09)
criteria.description: A custom cache abstraction in Application using the cache-aside pattern, implemented first with IMemoryCache and then with IDistributedCache via AddStackExchangeRedisCache, with expiration durations from CacheOptions (registered with ValidateOnStart). The Redis container (redis:alpine or valkey/valkey:alpine) runs and the application connects to it without runtime exceptions. Cached items: categories list, public campaign list pages and success stories, and campaign details GET /campaigns/{id} with sliding and absolute expiration. Keys include the language and all query parameters. Invalidation occurs immediately when a campaign is created, updated, deleted, or changes status, when a category changes, and when a donation succeeds. GET /donations/mine and any user-specific data are never cached under a shared key.

criteria.title: Bilingual Localization (ar / en, CMP-11)
criteria.description: Localization is configured with IStringLocalizer and .resx files, and the supported cultures en (default) and ar are resolved from the Accept-Language header with fallback to en. Accept-Language: ar outputs validation messages, error catalog messages (the Message of each Error inside ProblemDetails), and public fields (Title, Name, Description) in Arabic, while Accept-Language: en or no header outputs them in English. Admin and manager endpoints return both languages together. No hard-coded strings inside handlers, and stored data stays in Ar/En columns without automatic translation.

criteria.title: API Versioning & Rate Limiting
criteria.description: Versioning is via the URL segment /api/v1/... using Asp.Versioning.Mvc, and Scalar displays one OpenAPI document per version. The built-in Rate Limiter is configured with named policies whose limits come from RateLimitOptions (registered with ValidateOnStart): global for all endpoints partitioned per IP (default 100 requests/minute), auth on login, register, and refresh (10 requests/minute per IP), and donations on donation creation (20 requests/minute per user). Exceeding the limit returns 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header and a ProblemDetails body with code: Common.RateLimited. Middleware ordering is correct (UseRateLimiter after UseAuthentication so the user ID is available).

criteria.title: CORS Policy, Configuration & Secrets Protection
criteria.description: One named CORS policy in Program.cs, with origins from CorsOptions (validated on startup), along with explicit HTTP methods and headers. Never combine AllowAnyOrigin with AllowCredentials, and no hard-coded origins in code. No secrets in the repository or Git history: SQL Server and Redis connection strings and keys live in user-secrets or environment variables, and appsettings.json contains placeholders only.

criteria.title: Donation Unit Tests
criteria.description: New unit tests covering donation invariants: amount range, campaign must be active, final states cannot change (Donation.InvalidState), and campaign completion when the goal is reached. Also tests for the handlers: creating a donation, fetching own donation with 404 for another user's donation, and mark-succeeded (status, ReceiptNumber, and RaisedAmount). The repository and TimeProvider are faked (Moq [4.18.4] and FakeTimeProvider), and pinned package versions are respected (FluentAssertions [7.0.0] and MediatR [12.5.0]). All tests pass with dotnet test.

criteria.title: README & Submission
criteria.description: The README is updated for this sprint: what was added, how to try it (e.g., running Redis with Docker, configuring secrets via user-secrets, testing Accept-Language and 429), design decisions (e.g., how RaisedAmount was made concurrency-safe), and contains an explicit section for the cache invalidation strategy (keys, durations, and when each is invalidated). The tag named sprint-3 exists and points to the latest commit, and any fixes are placed on a tag named sprint-3-fix without moving the original.

criteria.title: Explaining Decisions & Trade-offs
criteria.description: The student's ability during review to explain the rationale behind their decisions, alternatives, and trade-offs, such as: how you made RaisedAmount concurrency-safe and why RowVersion with retry instead of ExecuteUpdateAsync (or vice versa), when a single SaveChangesAsync is sufficient versus when an explicit transaction is needed, how you guarantee ReceiptNumber uniqueness, why 404 and not 403 for another user's resource, why a role check alone is not enough to protect PUT /campaigns/{id}, why language is included in the cache key and how list pages are invalidated with IDistributedCache, why the donations policy is per user while auth is per IP, and why CORS is not server protection. Answers are graded on understanding rather than memorization.
